Today we see how alkenes, carbonyl compounds and Grignard reagents become alcohols, and how benzene becomes phenol. In this lesson: Prepare alcohols from alkenes, carbonyl compounds and Grignard reagents.
Prepare phenol from haloarenes, sulphonic acids, diazonium salts and cumene.

title.en: Alcohols from alkenes and carbonyl compounds

body.en: Acid-catalysed hydration adds water by Markovnikov’s rule (propene → propan-2-ol). Hydroboration–oxidation ($B_2H_6$, then $H_2O_2/OH^-$) adds it the other way (propene → propan-1-ol). Reduction with $H_2$/Pd, $NaBH_4$ or $LiAlH_4$ turns aldehydes into 1° *alcohols* and ketones into 2° alcohols; $LiAlH_4$ reduces carboxylic acids to 1° alcohols.
body.kn: ಆಮ್ಲ ಜಲಸಂಯೋಜನೆ ಮಾರ್ಕೋನಿಕಾಫ್ ನಿಯಮ ಪಾಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಹೈಡ್ರೋಬೋರೇಷನ್–ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಣ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಆಲ್ಕೋಹಾಲ್ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಆಲ್ಡಿಹೈಡ್ ಅಪಕರ್ಷಣದಿಂದ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ, ಕೀಟೋನ್ ಅಪಕರ್ಷಣದಿಂದ ದ್ವಿತೀಯಕ ಆಲ್ಕೋಹಾಲ್.

say.en: Acid-catalysed hydration of an alkene follows Markovnikov’s rule.
Hydroboration–oxidation adds water the other way round, so propene gives propan-1-ol.
Reducing a carbonyl group: aldehydes give primary alcohols and ketones give secondary alcohols.
A Grignard reagent adds to the carbonyl group and water then gives the alcohol. Methanal gives primary, other aldehydes secondary, ketones tertiary.
Worked example: methylmagnesium bromide and acetone give 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
Phenol is made from chlorobenzene under harsh conditions, or from cumene, which also gives acetone.
Routes to alcohols and phenol.

body.en: From chlorobenzene: NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, then acid. From benzenesulphonic acid: fuse with NaOH, then acidify. From benzenediazonium chloride: warm with water ($C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_5OH + N_2 + HCl$). From cumene: air oxidation to cumene hydroperoxide, then dilute acid gives *phenol* and acetone (the industrial method).

problem.en: What mass of phenol is obtained from 60 g of cumene (C₉H₁₂) by the cumene process, assuming 100% yield? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)

steps.en: C₆H₅CH(CH₃)₂ → C₆H₅C(CH₃)₂OOH → C₆H₅OH + CH₃COCH₃ (1 mol cumene gives 1 mol phenol).
Molar mass of cumene = 108 + 12 = 120 g/mol; 60 g = 0.5 mol.

answer.en: 47 g of phenol (and 29 g of acetone)

narration.en: Let us solve this together. What mass of phenol is obtained from 60 g of cumene (C₉H₁₂) by the cumene process, assuming 100% yield? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)

say.en: Let us solve this together. What mass of phenol is obtained from 60 grams of cumene C 9H 12 by the cumene process, assuming 100 percent yield? (C equals 12, H equals 1, O equals 16).
C 6H 5CHCH 3 2 gives C 6H 5CCH 3 2OOH gives C 6H 5OH plus CH 3COCH 3 (1 mole cumene gives 1 mole phenol).
Molar mass of cumene equals 108 plus 12 equals 120 grams per mole; 60 grams equals 0.5 moles.
Phenol C 6H 6O equals 94 grams per mole; mass equals 0.5 times 94 equals 47 grams.
So the answer is 47 grams of phenol and 29 grams of acetone.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Show how 2-methylpropan-2-ol can be made from a Grignard reagent.
The target CH 3 3C-OH is a 3 degrees alcohol, so start from a ketone.
CH 3MgBr plus CH 3COCH 3 gives CH 3 3C-OMgBr.
Hydrolysis: CH 3 3C-OMgBr plus H 2O gives CH 3 3C-OH plus MgOHBr.
So the answer is Methylmagnesium bromide plus propanone, then hydrolysis.

say.kn: ಗ್ರಿಗ್ನಾರ್ಡ್ plus HCHO gives 1 degrees, plus RCHO gives 2 degrees, plus R 2CO gives 3 degrees ಆಲ್ಕೋಹಾಲ್.

say.en: Cumene process gives phenol and acetone.
say.kn: ಕ್ಯೂಮೀನ್ ವಿಧಾನ ಫೀನಾಲ್ ಮತ್ತು ಅಸಿಟೋನ್ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.
